description: During an incident, commit to when people will next hear from you rather than when the problem will be fixed, and never adopt another party's estimate as your own commitment.
when_to_apply: people affected by an incident are asking when it will be fixed
a vendor or another team has given a fix estimate
someone proposes telling customers a resolution time
steps: Tell affected people what is affected, what you are doing, and the time of the next update.
Keep that update time even if the update is 'no change'.
If you pass on someone else's estimate, label it as theirs and say you are not relying on it.
Describe any workaround you control alongside the estimate you do not.
quality_indicators: every promised update time was met
no resolution time was given that the team did not control
later updates were believed rather than discounted
failure_modes: relaying a vendor ETA as your own and missing it, which discounts every later update
giving no time at all, which reads as not knowing what you are doing
example: A storage provider says its fix will land within the hour. Rather than telling customers it will be resolved by a specific time, the incident commander has them told that downloads are degraded, a workaround is rolling out, and the next update will come at the top of the hour whether or not it is fixed.
